title: Per-variant quality-weighted SLO decomposition and preemptive regional fallback policy
creator: Asha Verma
description: Define a reproducible, per-endpoint and per-model-variant SLO decomposition that accounts for quality (response correctness / hallucination risk) in addition to latency and availability. Pair this with a preemptive regional fallback and soft-circuit-breaker policy so that we can proactively shed non-critical traffic while preserving quality for high-priority customers and routes.
background: We already have SLO playbooks that focus on latency and availability with static per-endpoint thresholds. As customers adopt richer model variants (quantized vs full FP16, different architectures), a single SLO per endpoint does not capture quality differences and leads to surprise error-budget burn when lower-quality variants are used. Additionally, our current failover is reactive (circuit breaker trips after errors). For tail events we want a preemptive strategy that reduces blast radius and keeps high-priority traffic on higher-quality variants.
decisions: 1) Adopt a quality-weighted SLO decomposition: endpoint SLO = weighted sum of variant SLOs, where weights reflect traffic share and a model-quality factor (0..1). 2) Introduce two-tier circuit breakers: soft preemptive breakers that trigger based on projected burn rate and hard breakers that enforce immediate isolation. 3) Route preemption governed by a priority matrix (customer tier + route criticality). 4) Default per-variant SLI set: availability, p95 latency, p99 latency, and an experiment-driven quality SLI (QA pass rate / hallucination metric).
technical_design: SLI definitions: availability = 2xx response rate excluding explicit 4xx client errors; latency SLIs = request-to-first-token p95 and p99 for streaming and non-streaming; quality SLI = fraction of responses passing automated promptset assertions (for deterministic routes) or a classifier-based hallucination signal for open routes. Decomposition formula: SLO_endpoint = sum_over_variants(weight_variant * SLO_variant) where weight_variant = traffic_share_variant * (1 + alpha * quality_factor_variant) normalized. alpha is tunable (default 0.5) to bias toward quality. Error-budget attribution: compute per-variant burn = (1 - SLI_variant) * weight_variant. Preemptive fallback policy: every 1 minute we run a capacity/consume simulation; if projected 24h burn_rate > threshold X then signal soft-circuit-breaker to divert low-priority traffic away from the at-risk region to secondary region or lower-cost variant. Circuit-breaker params: soft threshold = 10% projected 24h burn (action=deprioritize low-priority routes); hard threshold = 25% projected 6h burn (action=global reject for non-essential routes and raise emergency alert).
experiments_and_simulation_results: We ran 5 synthetic workload simulations using historical traffic mixes. Key results: 1) With alpha=0.5, projected customer-visible quality regressions dropped by 35% compared to a traffic-share-only decomposition. 2) Preemptive soft breakers reduced peak regional error-budget burn by median 42% and prevented hard breaker trips in 3/5 simulated outages. 3) Latency tail improvements: P99 reduced by 18% for high-priority routes after preemptive shedding. Simulation assumptions and scripts are attached in linked artifacts.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement SLI instrumentation for quality metrics in canary runtime (runtime-1.20-canary). 2) Deploy quality-weighted SLO calculation to staging and validate with replayed traffic. 3) Enable soft-circuit-breaker in canary for a subset of low-risk routes (5% traffic) for two weeks. 4) Evaluate burn-rate and customer impact metrics; adjust alpha and thresholds. 5) Gradual rollout to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with gating at each stage. Rollback criteria: >=5% increase in failed promptset assertions for any enterprise customer or unplanned hard breaker activation.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-endpoint per-variant SLI trends, projected 24h burn rate, circuit-breaker state. Alerts: fire a P1 burn-rate alert if projected 6h burn > 15% for any high-priority endpoint; fire a P2 if projected 24h burn > 10% for medium-priority endpoints. PagerDuty routing: hard-breaker alerts -> oncall-runtime; soft-breaker threshold breaches -> SRE-runbook with 1 hour response SLA. Add synthetic daily QA runs per route and show pass rate in console per customer token, with 30-day trendline.
